interpretations: Only tracks with Bytes strictly greater than 10,323,804 are kept. For each media type, take the mean of the per-track Bytes/Milliseconds ratios. Then take the unweighted mean of those per-type means.
Only tracks with Bytes greater than or equal to 10,323,804 are kept. The rest is the same: the mean of per-track ratios within each media type, then the unweighted mean across types.
Only tracks with Bytes less than 10,323,804 are kept ("pass" read as staying under a limit). The rest is the same.
Only tracks with Bytes less than or equal to 10,323,804 are kept. The rest is the same.

Tracks above the cutoff are kept. Each media type's value is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds (ratio of sums) instead of the mean of per-track ratios. The result is the simple average of those per-type values.
Per-track Bytes ÷ Milliseconds uses floating-point division. The final value is unrounded.
Per-track Bytes ÷ Milliseconds uses integer division, which truncates, before averaging.
Media types with no tracks above the cutoff are excluded from the final average.
Media types with no tracks above the cutoff are counted as 0 in the final average.
Grouping is by MediaType.Name. Media types that share a name would be merged.
Grouping is by MediaTypeId, with the name used only as a label. The final average is over the distinct media types.
Tracks with NULL Bytes are excluded, which is the natural result of the cutoff comparison.
The cutoff is applied to the per-track ratio instead of to Bytes. This reading is unlikely, since the cutoff is described as a file-size cutoff.
The final average is the simple mean of the per-media-type averages. It is not weighted by track count.
The final average is weighted by track count, which makes it equal to the overall mean of the ratio. This conflicts with the "simple average" wording.
Tracks are filtered on the cutoff in every existing interpretation, so the missing ones are different places to apply it:
The cutoff is applied at the media-type level, keeping only media types whose average (or total) Bytes passes 10,323,804, rather than filtering individual tracks.
Each media type's value is the ratio of its average Bytes to its average Milliseconds, computed after the track filter. This is equivalent to the ratio of sums, but computed from averages.
Media types with no tracks at all are included through an outer join and counted as 0 or NULL, separately from types with no tracks above the cutoff.
